body:
Technically not needed for #5799 (just because no tests hit this), but a similar pattern had to be fixed for `KernelFunctionOperation` in that PR.  We saw before that splatting generators is bad for inference, `map` is more robust.

> The adapt rule of `SumOfArrays` splatted a generator over its arrays, which isn't inferable: the adapted type was `SumOfArrays{N, <:Tuple}` with abstract elements even for plain arrays. Where the rule runs inside a kernel, as KernelAbstractions does for `@Const` arguments, that doesn't compile. Mapping over the arrays tuple is inferable; `Base.Fix1` keeps the adaptor's type when it is a type, e.g. `Array`, which a closure would capture as a `DataType`.
title: Adapt `SumOfArrays` by mapping over its arrays

body:
Guess what?  Yes, this is also taken out of #5799

> GPUArrays 12 reduces through AcceleratedKernels, which takes a linear
> view of the source array (`@view src[begin:end]`), reshapes it, and
> adapts the result for the kernel. Reductions without a condition passed
> the `Field` itself, and a `Field` doesn't support any of this:
> `lastindex` is the last index of its halo'd data, a one-index `view` is
> an x-slice, and adapting it returns its data with halos, so the
> reshaped array no longer fits. Reductions now get the field's interior,
> a 1-based array of the field's own size, as the index reductions
> already do.
title: Reduce over the interior of fields

body:
Once again taken out of #5799.  This is in the same vein as #6227: generators are complicated for inference, instead `map` is more robust

> With GPUArrays 12, reductions over GPU arrays run AcceleratedKernels' kernels, which mark their source `@Const`. KernelAbstractions adapts `@Const` arguments inside the kernel, so the adapt rule of a `KernelFunctionOperation` being reduced runs in device code. The rule built the adapted arguments with `Tuple` of a generator, which collects into an `Array` and isn't inferable, and compiling the kernel failed with an `InvalidIRError`. Mapping over the arguments tuple is inferable and allocation-free.
title: Adapt `KernelFunctionOperation` arguments with `map`
